items.title: Twin-stick control panel eats roughly a third of the phone screen and breaks the warm HUD
items.what: Across every portrait gameplay shot (e.g. the LUNGE PUNCH frame, screenshot 5, and the neutral stance frame, screenshot 15) the lower ~30% of the 390x844 phone is a cold black panel holding two ~250px dual-stick dials. In the landscape capture (screenshot 9) the same panel balloons to nearly 40% of the screen height while dimmed and inactive, leaving a dead black band under the fight. The 'STANCE' and 'TECHNIQUE' word labels under each dial are redundant — every dial already prints up/down/left/right arrows at its cardinal points.
items.why: A phone player is forced to choose between watching the fight and seeing the action buttons. A 30% cold slab contradicts the warm tatami atmosphere the rest of the screen is selling, and a 40% slab in landscape is unforgivable real-estate waste. New players in the first five seconds will read the screen as 'mostly menus' before they ever throw a punch.
items.how: Shrink each stick to ~180px and recolor the panel to a warm translucent brown (roughly rgba(30,18,8,0.6)) so it melts into the tatami, or render each stick as a free-floating soft vignette with no backing panel. Drop the redundant 'STANCE'/'TECHNIQUE' word labels — the on-dial arrows already say it. In landscape, hide the panel entirely during active rounds and surface sticks on a 'tap to show controls' affordance, or auto-fade after 2s of input.

items.title: Moves and Settings panels leave the dual sticks visible underneath, eating scroll space
items.what: In the Moves list (screenshot 6) and the Settings list (screenshot 7) the dimmed twin-stick dials are still drawn at the bottom of the screen, taking up the same ~30% of vertical space as during play. The Moves list of 10 techniques is forced against a hard bottom edge, and the Settings list ends at 'Show performance HUD' with a huge empty void before the dimmed sticks.
items.why: Modal screens are the player's reference card and options menu — they should be fully readable. Sharing a 390x844 phone with dead controls means the Moves list is partially below the fold and Settings has an obvious empty void the player will read as a layout bug.
items.how: Hide (or fully fade to opacity 0) the control panel whenever a modal is open and let the modal content expand to fill the full height. Add internal scrolling inside the Moves list and a closing safe-area buffer so the last toggle ('Show performance HUD') and the last Moves row are reachable with a thumb.

items.title: Qualifier intro has weak type hierarchy and an unexplained 'FIGHT N' badge
items.what: On the Qualifier intro screen (screenshots 2, 11, 14) the bold gold sans-serif 'QUALIFIER' is paired with 'vs HasanAbi' in a thin white serif that visually fights it instead of supporting it. The tagline 'PATIENT. HE WAITS FOR YOUR WIND-UP — THEN MAKES YOU PAY.' sits in a tiny pill that is barely legible on a 390x844 phone. The big gold 'FIGHT' button carries a small numbered circle that reads '2', then '3', then '4' across attempts (screenshot 8 also shows 'REMATCH 8') with no legend, no round label, and no counter that the player can map it to.
items.why: This is the first impression of a bout. Mismatched typefaces read as a design bug, the tiny tagline is functionally invisible, and the numbered badge is a mystery the player has to ignore — or worse, distrust. The same unexplained number reappears on the Rematch button, reinforcing that it is decorative or, at best, a debug counter that leaked into the shipping UI.
items.how: Match 'vs HasanAbi' to the same sans-serif family as 'QUALIFIER' (a lighter weight is fine) so the lockup reads as one heading. Promote the tagline to a full-width translucent card with a larger type, or fold it into a single subtitle line. Replace the inner numbered circle on FIGHT/REMATCH with an undecorated tap target, or with an icon that actually labels what's happening — a '1/5' round counter or a clock glyph that explains the countdown.

items.title: ShoeMoney loading screen wastes most of the phone screen as empty black
items.what: Screenshot 1 places the diamond SM logo, 'SM KARATE KIDS' gold title, 'ASMONGOLD VS HASANABI' subtitle, 'Downloading the game' status, a thin gold progress bar, and the 'A SHOEMONEY AI LABS GAME' footer all in a tight vertical band that occupies roughly the middle 30% of a 390x844 portrait. The top ~35% and the bottom ~35% of the screen are pure black with nothing in them, and the progress bar has no percentage label.
items.why: This is the very first thing every player sees. The brand mark is fighting with empty void for attention, and on a 4G download that lasts many seconds the player is staring at a logo floating in blackness with only a thin line as feedback.
items.how: Either (a) push the cluster up and add a vertically-progressing visual — a tatami weave filling top-down, or a slow amber glow rising behind the logo — so the eye has somewhere to travel, or (b) letterbox the content to a 16:9 block centred on a textured warm vignette so the screen never reads as empty. Add a percentage label next to the progress bar so the bar visibly moves.

items.title: IPPON hit effect reads as face paint, not impact
items.what: On the 'IPPON / HASANABI / SPINNING BACK KICK' KO screen (screenshot 12) the impact effect renders as three bright yellow, sharp-edged lightning-bolt sprites sitting on Asmongold's face and hair. They are unblurred, high-contrast, and static, and they sit on the head rather than radiating from the contact point (HasanAbi's foot against the chest).
items.why: This is the biggest beat in the game — a one-hit KO — and the rest of the frame works hard to sell a warm, cinematic dojo. The opaque yellow sprites look like UI marks or face paint glued to the character, breaking the photographic illusion and reading as a rendering bug rather than a hit.
items.how: Replace the sprite bolts with a TSL-driven bloom flash that emanates from the actual contact point (the chest, where the kick lands), a short radial chromatic-aberration pulse, and a single motion-blurred contact frame. If a lightning shape is wanted, render it as a soft additive flare that animates outward and fades in ~200ms, instead of an opaque decal parked on the face.
